content: A funeral home, also known as a mortuary, is a business establishment that provides services related to the burial and funeral of deceased individuals. These services are designed to support both the deceased and their families during the process of saying goodbye. Funeral homes often organize wakes and funeral ceremonies, and they may also provide a chapel for these services. They handle essential administrative tasks, such as completing necessary paperwork, obtaining permits, coordinating with cemeteries, and submitting obituaries to local media outlets. In the United States, there are several common types of funeral services. A traditional funeral service typically includes a viewing or wake, a funeral ceremony held at a church or the funeral home’s chapel, and a graveside committal service. Direct cremation involves the funeral home receiving the deceased’s remains, completing the required legal documentation, and carrying out the cremation process without a formal ceremony. Direct or immediate burial occurs when the family opts to forgo a funeral service and instead arranges for the deceased to be buried promptly. In cases where the deceased needs to be transported to or from another location, such as a different state or country, the funeral home prepares the body for shipment. When a body is brought to the funeral home, embalming is sometimes performed to slow the natural process of decomposition. Embalming typically involves replacing the blood with a mixture of preservative chemicals and dyes, aspirating the internal organs, and setting the facial features of the deceased. Makeup is often applied to give the deceased a more lifelike appearance. If the individual’s body has been disfigured due to an accident or illness, restorative techniques may be used to make the body suitable for an open-casket service. If restoration is not possible or if the family prefers, a closed-casket service can be arranged. Funeral homes often provide designated spaces for visitations, where family and friends can gather to pay their respects. These areas may include a viewing room where the deceased is displayed in their casket. Funeral or memorial services may also be conducted on-site at the funeral home. Many funeral homes offer prearrangement services, allowing individuals to plan their own funeral arrangements in advance. With the growing popularity of cremation, some funeral homes now have on-site crematoriums, while others outsource cremation services to specialized facilities. Funeral homes can vary in ownership. Some are family-owned and operated, while others are part of larger corporate entities. Interestingly, corporate-owned funeral homes often operate under the guise of being family-owned to maintain a personal and community-oriented image. One of the largest corporations in the funeral industry is Service Corporation International. In popular culture, funeral homes have been depicted in various forms of media. The television series Six Feet Under portrayed a fictional funeral home, while the show Family Plots documented the real-life operations of a funeral home in California. The movie My Girl featured a character, Harry Sultenfuss (played by Dan Aykroyd), who ran a mortuary from his home. Additionally, in the Lifetime TV movie Wisegal, a mafia captain named Frank Russo used a funeral home as a front for his criminal activities.
